headline: A 2013 law let the Transportation Secretary move federal airport and FAA funds into air traffic control accounts for fiscal year 2013 to reduce flight delays.
what_it_does: The law allowed the Secretary of Transportation to shift money for fiscal year 2013 from airport grant programs and other FAA programs into FAA operating accounts, such as the one for air traffic control. The transfer could override the existing 2013 spending law and any sequestration order. Money moved this way became available right away to spend. The Secretary had to notify Congress at least five days before any transfer.

who_it_affects.how: The law was aimed at reducing flight delays by putting more money toward air traffic control operations.

who_it_affects.group: Airports receiving federal airport improvement grants
who_it_affects.how: Grant money in the airport improvement program could be reduced or redirected to FAA operations for fiscal year 2013.

who_it_affects.group: Air traffic controllers and FAA staff
who_it_affects.how: Funding for air traffic control operations could increase during fiscal year 2013 because of the transfer authority.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 1, 2013, and applied to fiscal year 2013 funds.
